name: Auxiliary session action only (sts:TagSession) with Principal '*' - session-control, NOT public assume
note: IAM-805 iteration 3 blocking-defect regression. A statement whose ONLY action is an auxiliary session action (sts:TagSession) grants no ability to assume the role, even with Principal '*'. It must be classified as an informational session-control capability, NEVER a critical TRUST-PUBLIC 'any principal may assume' finding (that asserts an assumption the action does not grant - threat-model T8).
rationale: sts:TagSession only PERMITS passing session tags on an assume; it is required in the trust policy for a caller/IdP to pass session tags, but it grants nothing on its own (trust-policy-semantics 3, source 8). AWS evaluates the assume action and the auxiliary session action for the SAME caller, so a principal that cannot already assume this role via a separate sts:AssumeRole* grant never reaches sts:TagSession - the statement is inert. Even with Principal '*' there is no assume grant here, so classifying it as public/anonymous role trust ('any principal may assume') would assert an assumption the action does not convey (threat-model T8). The correct classification is an informational session-control capability with prose that never claims assumption. Ref: AWS Pass session tags in STS (sts:TagSession); docs/trust-policy-semantics.md sec 3.
